title: Europe beyond France
lead: Advanced Europe sorts the map into buckets: Piedmont and Tuscany in depth, Germany’s small regions and VDP rules, Portugal past the Douro, Austria and Greece, the East, and the newer countries on the Court’s list.

intro.title: BIG BUCKETS, SMALL BUCKETS
intro.text: The Court lists dozens of places in this chapter. Give the classic regions the most time, then learn one clear fact for each smaller one.

tiers.name: One fact each
tiers.note: The East, England, Switzerland, the Middle East, Asia

sections.name: Italy
sections.source: Court of Master Sommeliers, Advanced Theory Exam guide; Consorzio di Tutela Barolo Barbaresco Alba Langhe e Dogliani; Consorzio Vino Chianti Classico

lines.label: Twenty regions
lines.text: The Court lists all twenty Italian regions, from Valle d’Aosta to Sardinia. Its own study advice: give Piedmont and Tuscany far more time than Basilicata or Molise.

lines.label: Names inside the zone
lines.text: Top Italian zones now name smaller places on the label. Barolo’s vineyard names (MGA) entered its rules in 2010. Chianti Classico has drawn eleven UGAs, used first only on Gran Selezione.

chips.label: Barolo communes wholly inside the zone

know: Barolo comes from 11 communes; only Barolo, Serralunga d’Alba and Castiglione Falletto lie wholly inside the zone.
Barolo ages at least three years, a year and a half in wood; Riserva needs five.
Barbaresco comes from Barbaresco, Neive, Treiso and part of Alba; it ages two years, nine months in oak, and Riserva four.
Chianti Classico covers 71,800 ha between Florence and Siena, including all of Castellina, Gaiole, Greve and Radda.
The Chianti Classico consorzio was founded in Radda in Chianti on May 14, 1924, under the Black Rooster.

sections.name: Germany
sections.source: Wines of Germany (Deutsches Weininstitut); VDP.Die Prädikatsweingüter; Court of Master Sommeliers, Advanced Theory Exam guide

lines.label: Thirteen regions
lines.text: The Court lists all 13 German regions. Five have under 1,000 ha; the Mittelrhein, at 439 ha, is the smallest.

lines.label: The 2021 law
lines.text: German law now ranks PDO wine by origin: wine region, then Region, then village, then single vineyard. The rules bind from the 2026 vintage, and the Prädikat levels stay the same.

know: Sachsen is the easternmost region, 531 ha, with vines starting near Dresden at 51° north.
Saale-Unstrut is the northernmost quality region; Pinot Blanc and Müller-Thurgau lead its 868 ha.
Württemberg is 63% red: Lemberger (1,661 ha) just ahead of Trollinger (1,614 ha).
A VDP.Grosses Gewächs is a dry wine from a VDP.Grosse Lage, from at most 50 hl/ha, picked by hand.
GG whites go on sale September 1 the year after harvest; GG reds a year later, after 12 months or more in oak.

rows.name: VDP.Grosse Lage
rows.note: max 50 hl/ha · dry wine = Grosses Gewächs

rows.name: VDP.Gutswein
rows.note: max 75 hl/ha · the estate’s own vineyards

sections.name: Spain and Portugal
sections.source: Consejo Regulador DOCa Rioja; Spain’s Ministry of Agriculture (MAPA); Wines of Portugal; Court of Master Sommeliers curriculum guide

lines.label: Spain
lines.text: The Court asks for all of Spain’s major regions plus Vino de Pago. Rioja now has its own single-vineyard tier, Viñedo Singular, approved by the ministry vineyard by vineyard.

lines.label: Portugal
lines.text: Wines of Portugal maps 14 regions and counts more than 250 native grapes. Advanced goes past the Douro to the south and the islands.

know: Bairrada is clay-limestone and sand; its classic reds are Baga, and it was an early home of Portuguese sparkling.
Távora-Varosa was the first region demarcated for DOC sparkling wine, in 1989.
In Lisboa, Bucelas is Arinto, and Colares is Ramisco planted in loose sand by the sea.
Palmela reds are Castelão on warm sand; Moscatel de Setúbal is the region’s famous fortified wine.
The Azores have three appellations, Graciosa, Biscoitos and Pico, with vines in volcanic stone corrals.

rows.name: Colares
rows.meta: Ramisco on sand by the sea

sections.name: Austria, Greece and Eastern Europe
sections.source: Vinea Wachau; Weinviertel DAC; Wine Burgenland; Wine Styria; Wines of Greece; bor.hu; UNESCO; Wine Folly

lines.label: Austria
lines.text: The Court names four Austrian areas: Niederösterreich, Wien, Steiermark and Burgenland. The Wachau and Styria layer their DACs from region to village to single vineyard.

lines.label: Greece and the East
lines.text: Greece’s classic PDOs date from 1971. Further east, the Court lists Slovenia, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Georgia and Russia.

know: Wachau DAC has three levels, Gebietswein, Ortswein and Riedenwein, all hand-picked; a Riedenwein is only Grüner Veltliner or Riesling.
Leithaberg DAC wines grow on shell limestone; Mittelburgenland DAC is Blaufränkisch.
Mantinia PDO is at least 85% Moschofilero from a cold plateau about 660 m up; it can be still or sparkling.
Santorini’s Nykteri is dry, at least 13.5% alcohol, with at least 3 months in oak.
Georgia’s qvevri winemaking, in buried egg-shaped clay jars, joined UNESCO’s intangible heritage list in 2013.

items.name: Mantinia
items.text: Moschofilero, one of the coldest PDOs

sections.name: England, Switzerland, the Middle East and Asia
sections.source: WineGB; Swiss Wine Promotion; Cyprus Food Museum; China Daily; Wine Folly; Court of Master Sommeliers, Advanced Theory Exam guide

lines.label: England and Switzerland
lines.text: England’s vines run from Cornwall to Yorkshire; the five biggest counties are Sussex, Kent, Essex, Hampshire and Surrey. Switzerland groups 26 cantons and 62 AOCs into six regions.

lines.label: Middle East and Asia
lines.text: The Court lists Israel, Lebanon and Cyprus, then China and India. Cyprus’s Commandaria and China’s Ningxia have the clearest rules and stories.

know: In England, eastern counties like Essex and Kent are warmer and give riper grapes.
Valais holds almost one-third of Swiss vineyards; Vaud calls itself the home of Chasselas.
Commandaria uses only Xynisteri and Mavro, from unirrigated vines at least four years old, sun-dried before pressing.
Commandaria must ferment inside the 14 designated villages.
Ningxia growers bury their vines before winter and dig them up in spring.

Over 40% of China’s wine
Cabernet Gernischt, Marselan

facts.fact: Court Advanced topics: Italy (Piedmont, Valle d’Aosta, Liguria, Lombardy, Trentino-Alto Adige, Veneto, Friuli-Venezia-Giulia, Emilia-Romagna, Tuscany, Marche, Umbria, Lazio, Molise, Abruzzo, Campania, Basilicata, Puglia, Calabria, Sicily, Sardinia); Germany (13 regions); Spain (all major regions, Vino de Pago); Portugal (all major regions and styles); Greece (all major regions and styles); Other Europe (England, Switzerland); Austria (Niederösterreich, Wien, Steiermark, Burgenland); Eastern Europe & Caucasus/Russia (Slovenia, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Georgia, Russia); Middle East (Israel, Lebanon, Cyprus); Asia (China, India).
Court study strategy: when studying Italy, budget proportionately more time for Tuscany and Piedmont than for Basilicata or Molise.

Barolo DOCG: 100% Nebbiolo; 11 municipalities; Barolo, Serralunga d’Alba and Castiglione Falletto wholly included; La Morra, Monforte, Verduno, Novello, Grinzane Cavour, Diano d’Alba, Cherasco and Roddi partly included.
Barolo ages at least three years (beyond the two months after harvest), one and a half in oak; Riserva after five years.
Barolo’s Additional Geographical Mentions (MGA) were delimited and recognized in the production rules in 2010.
Barbaresco DOCG: 100% Nebbiolo from Barbaresco, Neive, Treiso and part of Alba; at least two years of aging, nine months in oak; Riserva after four years.
Chianti Classico zone: 71,800 ha between Florence and Siena; includes all of Castellina, Gaiole, Greve and Radda in Chianti and parts of other communes.
The Chianti Classico consorzio began in Radda in Chianti on May 14, 1924, under the Black Rooster.
Chianti Classico has eleven Additional Geographic Units (UGA) to be shown on labels, applicable in the first phase only to Gran Selezione.
Sachsen: easternmost German region, 531 ha, vines begin near Dresden at 51° N; Riesling is now its most important grape.
Saale-Unstrut: Germany’s northernmost quality region, 868 ha (2025), about 500 mm of rain; largest of the five regions under 1,000 ha; Pinot Blanc (116 ha) and Müller-Thurgau (110 ha) lead.
Mittelrhein: Germany’s smallest region (2025), 439 ha; clayish slate and greywacke; Riesling leads.
Hessische Bergstraße: 440 ha; an independent region since 1971.
Württemberg: 10,694 ha, 63% red; Lemberger 1,661 ha, Trollinger 1,614 ha; over 50 cooperatives market about 80% of its wine.
Nahe soils include slate, volcanic porphyry, loess and loam.

The 10th amendment to the German Wine Act took effect January 27, 2021; within PDO wines a four-level origin pyramid (wine-growing region, Region, municipality, single vineyard); binding from the 2026 vintage; Prädikat levels unchanged.

VDP four-tier classification (Gutswein, Ortswein, Erste Lage, Grosse Lage) adopted in January 2012. Max yields: Grosse Lage 50 hl/ha, Erste Lage 60, Ortswein 75, Gutswein 75. Grosse Lage and Erste Lage are hand-harvested.

Dry wines from VDP.Grosse Lage sites are VDP.Grosses Gewächs; sweet ones carry the Prädikat names. GG whites are released September 1 the year after harvest; GG reds September 1 of the second year after harvest, with at least 12 months in oak; sweet Grosse Lage wines May 1 the year after harvest.
Rioja has a Viñedo Singular (single vineyard) category; Spain’s agriculture ministry recognizes new Viñedos Singulares in DOCa Rioja.
Spain’s DOP tiers include Vino de Pago, DOCa and DO; Rioja and Priorat are the only DOCa.

Wines of Portugal lists 14 wine regions: Vinho Verde, Trás-os-Montes, Porto e Douro, Távora-Varosa, Dão e Lafões, Bairrada, Beira Interior, Lisboa, Tejo, Península de Setúbal, Alentejo, Algarve, Madeira, Açores. Távora-Varosa was the first region demarcated for DOC sparkling wine, in 1989.
Portugal has more than 250 native grape varieties.
Alentejo: hot, dry Mediterranean climate with continental influence; eight sub-regions: Borba, Évora, Granja-Amareleja, Moura, Portalegre, Redondo, Reguengos, Vidigueira.
Bairrada: clay-limestone and sandy soils; one of the first regions to make sparkling; classic wines from Baga; Fernão Pires is called Maria Gomes there; cool, humid climate.
Dão: mountains on all sides, poor granite soils, vineyards among pine forests from 1,000 m in the Serra da Estrela down to 200 m.
Lisboa has nine sub-regions; Bucelas (Arinto whites), Colares (Ramisco planted by the sea on loose sand) and Carcavelos stand out.
Península de Setúbal: birthplace of Moscatel de Setúbal; Palmela reds based on Castelão on warm sandy soils.
Açores: three appellations, Graciosa, Biscoitos and Pico; vines planted inside volcanic stone corrals; Verdelho is the most famous grape.
Certified curriculum (Spain) covers Rioja, Ribera, Priorat, Galicia and other DOs; Priorat bush vines on llicorella.
Wachau DAC: Gebietswein, Ortswein, Riedenwein; 100% hand-harvested; Riedenwein only Grüner Veltliner or Riesling.
Styria’s DAC pyramid runs from regional to village to single-vineyard wines; Schilcher and Sauvignon Blanc are named styles.
Burgenland DACs: Neusiedlersee, Leithaberg (shell limestone), Ruster Ausbruch, Rosalia (rosé), Mittelburgenland (Blaufränkisch), Eisenberg.
PDO Santorini (1971): at least 85% Assyrtiko with Athiri and Aidani; self-rooted vines; kouloura basket training; Nykteri is dry, at least 13.5% alcohol and at least 3 months in oak.
PDO Naoussa (1971): 100% Xinomavro on the south-eastern slopes of Mt Vermio.
PDO Nemea (1971): 100% Agiorgitiko, about 230–850 m; Greece’s largest PDO zone for red wine.

PDO Mantinia (1971): plateau at about 660 m, vineyards up to 800 m; one of the coldest PDO zones in Greece; at least 85% Moschofilero with Asproudes; still or sparkling; pink-grey hue and rose-like aromas.
Retsina is Greece’s best-known traditional wine, flavored with pine resin.
Since 2013, Tokaji Aszú needs at least 120 g/L of sugar and 18 months in wooden casks.
Egri Bikavér must be at least three grapes, at least 50% a native red, typically Kékfrankos (Kadarka also qualifies); Egri Csillag (‘Star of Eger’) is the white sister blend.
Bulgaria: Mavrud is native; Melnik 55 is Broad-leafed Melnik × Valdiguié from the Struma Valley; Rubin is Nebbiolo × Syrah; Gamza is Kadarka.

Qvevri wine-making was inscribed in 2013 on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity; the qvevri is an egg-shaped earthenware vessel used for making, ageing and storing wine.

English vineyards run from Cornwall to Yorkshire, Wales to the Isle of Wight, and recently Scotland; the five largest-producing counties are Sussex, Kent, Essex, Hampshire and Surrey; eastern counties like Essex and Kent are warmer and give higher sugar.
WineGB manages the UK Wine Schemes (PDO/PGI) on behalf of Defra.
Switzerland: 26 cantons and 62 wine AOCs grouped into six regions (Valais, Vaud, German-speaking Switzerland, Geneva, Ticino, Three Lakes); Valais has almost one-third of Swiss vineyards.
Vaud presents itself as the home of Chasselas; its AOC areas include Chablais, Lavaux, La Côte, Bonvillars and Côte de l’Orbe.

Commandaria: only Xynisteri and Mavro; vineyards at least four years old; irrigation prohibited; grapes overripen on the vine, then sun-dry until 19–23 Baumé; fermentation within the fourteen designated villages; alcohol up to 15%.
Helan Mountain in Ningxia lies between 37 and 39° N and has the most wineries in China; vines are buried before winter and unearthed in spring.

Shandong: maritime, monsoon rain, high disease pressure; over 40% of China’s wine; Cabernet Gernischt, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon. Ningxia: Helan Mountains by the Gobi, arid. Marselan (Cabernet Sauvignon × Grenache, bred 1961) resists powdery mildew, suiting Shandong.
Xinomavro is often compared to Nebbiolo; Malagousia makes aromatic whites.

unverified: Vino de Pago count: a search summary gave 27 for 2024/25 from a MAPA report, while other pages give 19, 20 or 24. No number is stated.
Rioja Viñedo Singular rules (vines at least 35 years old, yield caps, number approved) were only seen in search summaries, not read on the page. Only the category’s existence is stated.
Wien (Wiener Gemischter Satz DAC), Steiermark’s individual DACs, Slovenia, Romania, Russia, Israel, Lebanon and India: no official page was read this pass, so they are only named as Court topics.
Lebanon’s Bekaa Valley altitude (about 1,000 m and up) came from search summaries of producer pages, not read directly. Not stated.
Commandaria: PDO year (1990) and drying times (a week to 12 days) come from secondary pages and disagree. Not stated.
Wine Folly calls Tokaj ‘the oldest classified wine region in the world’, while Level 1 calls the Douro (1756) the oldest demarcated region. Neither claim is repeated here.
Wine Folly’s China page dates Changyu’s start to 1982, which looks like a typo for an earlier year. Not stated.
Chianti Classico’s UGA page still reads as if approval were pending; the date the UGAs took effect was not confirmed. No date is stated.
The austrianwine.com pages refused automated access (HTTP 403), so Austrian DAC dates are not given.

read.bigIdea: Small producers, each with one story to know.
read.where: The Court’s last European group is **England** and **Switzerland**. Then come the **Middle East** (Israel, Lebanon, Cyprus) and **Asia** (China, India). Israel, Lebanon and India are named here only as study targets.

stops.name: England
stops.text: **WineGB** runs the UK’s PDO and PGI schemes. The east, like **Essex** and **Kent**, is warmer and gives riper grapes.

stops.name: Switzerland
stops.text: 26 cantons and 62 **AOCs**. **Valais** has almost a third of the vines; **Vaud**, with **Lavaux** and **La Côte**, is the home of **Chasselas**.

stops.name: Cyprus
stops.text: Only **Xynisteri** and **Mavro**, unirrigated, sun-dried to 19–23 **Baumé**, fermented within the 14 villages.

stops.name: China
stops.text: **Ningxia** sits under the **Helan Mountains**, dry, and vines are buried each winter. Wet coastal **Shandong** suits mildew-resistant **Marselan**.

read.mixup: **Marselan** is Cabernet Sauvignon crossed with Grenache. **Cabernet Gernischt** is a different red planted in Shandong.
read.sayIt: Commandaria: a sweet amber wine from sun-dried Cypriot grapes.
